Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 36
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: South Asian
  relationship_status: Divorced
  occupation: Accountant
  trauma_type: Witnessed domestic violence (childhood)
  pcl5: 69

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Threat: Physical Reactivity: Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience, Body on Alert: My body feels constantly tense and ready to react to danger, Hypervigilance: Being superalert or watchful or on guard
  Memory: Terror on Recall: Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time, Nonverbal Memory: I can't seem to put the frightening event into words., Triggered Without Warning: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
  Negative Appraisals: No Accountability: The people responsible have faced no consequences, Lost Happiness: I used to be a happy person but now I am always miserable., Helplessness: I can't stop bad things from happening to me

Vignette:
Rohan's eyes would often glaze over when he recounted his childhood. He had grown up in a household where violence was a regular occurrence, with his father frequently lashing out at his mother. One particular incident stood out in his mind - the night his father had smashed a vase on the floor, mere inches from his mother's face. The sound of shattering glass still echoed in Rohan's mind, transporting him back to that moment of sheer terror. As he grew older, Rohan began to notice that certain triggers would set off a chain reaction within him. A raised voice, a slammed door, or even the faint scent of his father's cologne could send his body into high alert, his heart racing and muscles tensed, as if preparing for an imminent attack. These physical reactions left him feeling drained and on edge, always waiting for the next blow to fall. Rohan struggled to verbalize his memories of that fateful night, often finding himself at a loss for words when attempting to recount the events. The terror he felt upon recall was palpable, as if he were reliving the experience all over again. His inability to articulate these emotions only added to his frustration and sense of helplessness. As an accountant, Rohan's job required him to be meticulous and detail-oriented, but his hypervigilance often made it difficult for him to focus on tasks at hand. He would find himself scanning the office for potential threats or distractions, making it hard to concentrate on numbers and spreadsheets. His colleagues began to notice a change in him, how he seemed more withdrawn and anxious than before. Rohan's divorce had also been a significant blow, leaving him feeling like he was losing control of his life. He couldn't shake the feeling that he was powerless to stop bad things from happening to those around him, just as he had been unable to protect his mother all those years ago. The fact that his father had faced no consequences for his actions only added to Rohan's sense of injustice and despair. As time went on, Rohan became increasingly withdrawn, pushing away friends and family who tried to reach out to him. He felt like he was losing himself in the process, unable to recall a time when he wasn't plagued by these dark thoughts and feelings. His happiness seemed like a distant memory, replaced by an all-consuming sense of misery. One day, as Rohan was working late in the office, a colleague slammed a door shut, sending him into a panic. It was then that he realized he couldn't keep living like this - constantly on edge, unable to escape the ghosts of his past. He knew he needed help, but what frightened him most was the prospect of confronting those memories head-on. Would he be able to find a way to heal and move forward, or would these demons continue to haunt him forever?
